τοὺς βουνοὺς, ἵνα εἴπῃ, μὴ τὰ πρὸ τῆς κτίσεως ἐπίστασαι. Κεφ. Ι ʹ, ιηʹ, ιθʹ. Γῆς, μὴ
ἐπικαλύψῃς ἐφ' αἵ ματι τῆς σαρκός μου, μηδὲ εἴη τόπος τῇ κραυγῇ μου· καὶ νῦν ἰδοὺ
ἐν οὐρανοῖς ὁ μάρ τυς μου, ὁ δὲ συνίστωρ μου ἐν ὑψίστοις. Ἀπορούμενος πρὸς τὴν
γῆν διαλέγεται, 365 καὶ εἰς συμπάθειαν ἐκκαλούμενος λέγει ῥή ματα, ἃ καὶ εὐκτικῶς
εἴρηται. Λέγει δέ· Μὴ σιωπήσῃς, ὦ γῆ, τὰ κατ' ἐμὲ, μηδὲ συγ κρύψῃς τὸ ἀδίκως
ἐκχεόμενον αἷμα ἐκ τῆς σαρκός μου διὰ τῶν ἰχώρων· μηδὲ στῇ ἐν τόπῳ καὶ
ἀποκρυβῇ, μηδὲ εἰς λήθην ἔλθῃ τὰ κατὰ τοὺς ἐμοὺς ὀδυρμούς· πολλοὶ δὲ, φησὶν,
οἰκοδομήθωσαν διὰ τῶν ἐμῶν πειρασ μῶν. Ἢ μὴ γῆ κρύψῃ μου τὸ αἷμα, ἀλλ' ἐκ
καλέσηται τὸν Θεὸν εἰς ἐκδικίαν, αὐτοὺς τοῦ σώματος τοὺς ἰχῶρας ἔχουσα
μάρτυρας. Καὶ ὁ ἀὴρ μὴ ἐπισχοίη μου τὴν κραυγὴν, ἀλλ' εἰς οὐρανοὺς φθάσοι τῆς
φωνῆς ὁ τόνος, ἵνα ὁ Θεὸς τῶν γινομένων κακῶν ἔκδικος κατα στὰς, καὶ τοὺς
αἰτίους ἀμυνόμενος, οὕτω γοῦν ἅπασι δείξῃ τῶν ἐμοὶ βεβιωμένων τὸ ἄμεμπτον. Τὸ
δέ· Ἰδοὺ ἐν οὐρανοῖς ὁ μάρτυς μου, καθαρωτάτης ἐστὶ συνειδήσεως. Κεφ. ΙΘʹ, γʹ.
Γνῶτε μόνον ὅτι ὁ Κύριος ἐποίησε με οὕτως. Εἰς φόβον αὐτοὺς καταφέρει, οἱονεὶ
λέγων· Μὴ οὕτως ἐπεμβαίνετέ μοι κάμνοντι, μηδὲ ὑμεῖς τοῖς αὐτοῖς περιπέσητε, τὴν
αὐτὴν ἔχοντες φύσιν. δʹ, εʹ. Ναὶ δὴ ἐπ' ἀληθείας ἐγὼ ἐπλανή θην· παρ' ἐμοὶ δὲ
αὐλίζεται πλάνος, λαλῆσαι ῥήματα ἃ οὐκ ἔδει, τὰ δὲ ῥήματά μου πλα νᾶται, καὶ οὐκ
ἐπὶ καιροῦ. –Ἔα δὲ ὅτι ἐπ' ἐμοὶ μεγαλύνεσθε, ἐνάλλεσθε δέ μοι ὀνεί δει. ∆εδόσθω,
φησὶν, καθ' ὑπόθεσιν ὅτι πε πλάνημαι. Παρ' ἐμοὶ δὲ αὐλίζεται πλάνος· πλάνος ὁ
διάβολός ἐστιν. Τίς ὑμῖν, φησὶν, ἐκ τούτου βλάβη, ποία δὲ ἀνάγκη κρίνειν ὡς ἀσεβῆ,
καὶ ἐπεμβαίνειν πάσχοντι; δέον συγγινώσκειν ὑπὸ ἀλγηδόνων φθεγγομένῳ. –Εἰ καὶ
τοιαῦτα ἐπεποιήκειν οἷα οὐκ ἔδει, 366 ἆρ' οὖν ἐχρῆν ὑμᾶς οὕτω μοι ὀνειδίζειν; – Καὶ
δέον με, φησὶ, πάλαι εὐσεβείας ἐπιμε λούμενον, νῦν τὴν ἐκ τῶν ἔργων ἔχειν παῤ
ῥησίαν. Τοῦτο μὲν οὐ πεποίηκα, κρίνομαι δὲ ὡς πλάνος. Ἐπιβάλλει καὶ ὧδε· ʹ, ζʹ.
Γνῶτε οὖν ὅτι ὁ Κύριός ἐστιν ὁ ταράξας· ὀχύρωμα δὲ αὐτοῦ ἐπ' ἐμὲ ὕψωσεν. Ἰδοὺ
γελῶ ὀνείδει, οὐ λαλήσω. Κεκράξομαι, καὶ οὐδαμοῦ κρίμα. ∆ιαλογίζεσθε, φησίν· οὐκ
ἀπὸ σκοποῦ ἀλ γύνομαι, καθάπερ τειχίῳ τινὶ τοῖς δεινοῖς κυκλούμενος. Λέγω, φησὶν,
μετὰ ἀληθείας, ὡς ἔχει τὰ κατ' ἐμὲ, καὶ οὐ παραδέχεσθε τοὺς λόγους. Τὸ γὰρ ἐν
ὀνείδει, ἵνα εἴπῃ τὰ πράγματα. Τὸ δὲ οὐ λαλήσω, ἀντὶ τοῦ· διὰ τὸ ἀντιλέγειν μοι
ὑμᾶς δοκῶ μηδὲν εἰρη κέναι. –Εἰ δὲ καὶ πρὸς τὸν Θεὸν βοήσω, εἰς φανερὸν ἅπασιν
ἐνέγκαι τὰ κατ' ἐμὲ, οὐ τυγχάνω τῆς ἱκεσίας. Οὐδεὶς ἀκούει, οὐ δεὶς δικάζει, οὐδένα
βλέπω, οὐκ ἔχω ποῖ ἀπελθεῖν. Ταῦτα ἐλεῆσαι οὐ χρῆ; –Τοι γαροῦν ἀφήσητε, οὕτως
ἀκρίτως μου κατη γοροῦντες, μήποτε Θεὸς εἰς κρίσιν κασταστή σῃ, εἰς πράξεσθαι
ὑμῖν δίκην ἀλόγου θρα σύτητος. –Οὐ γὰρ ἀνεύθυνα, φησὶ, τὰ τοιαῦτα καταλιμπάνει
Θεός. Ἔσεσθαι γάρ φησιν, εἴτε κινηθείη καθ' ὑμῶν, ὡς ἀνονήτως ὑμῖν ἐμφαίνεται ἡ
ἐπὶ γνώσει τοῦ καλοῦ οἴησις, καὶ ἡ ἐπὶ τοῖς προσοῦσιν ἄδεια. – Α. Σ. Τί φατε [ὅτι] ἐν
πονηρίᾳ ὢν ταῦτα πάσχω, καὶ ὑμεῖς τὰ αὐτὰ φοβεῖσθαι ὀφεί λετε. –Ἐσπεύσατε ἂν,
φησὶ, τότε καίτοι πραγμάτων μαρτυρούντων ἐν λόγοις· ἐν λό γοις οὖν λάβεσθε ὡς
ἂν μηδὲ ὑπὸ τῆς ἀλη θείας ψηφίσασθαι ἀνεύθυνον. –Ὁ γοῦν ἑβραῖος καὶ ἁμάρτημα
λόγου ἔχει. Κεφ. Κʹ, ιʹ. Τοὺς υἱοὺς αὐτοῦ ὀλέσαισαν ἥττονες, αἱ δὲ χεῖρες αὐτοῦ
πυρσεύσαισαν ὀδύνας. 367 Καὶ οἱ πρότερον, φησὶν, ὑποδεέστεροι, τῶν τοῦ
παρανόμου παίδων καθέξουσι. ιεʹ. Πλοῦτος ἀδίκως συναγόμενος ἐξεμε θήσεται, ἐξ
οἰκίας αὐτοῦ ἐξελκύσει αὐτὸν ἄγγελος. Πάντα μὲν ὁ ἀσεβὴς πράττει ὥστε τὰ
ἀλλότρια λαβεῖν, καὶ πρὸς τοῦτον βλέπει τὸν σκοπὸν τὰ γενόμενα· ἐπειδὰν δὲ
ἐγκράτης τῶν ὅλων δόξῃ, τότ' αὑτὸν εἰς ἑτέρους με ταφερόμενον ὄψεται. ιηʹ. Ὥσπερ
στρείφνος ἀμάσητος, ἀκατά ποτος. Οἱ λόγοι καὶ τὰ δόγματα [ἀσεβοῦς] στρί φινα καὶ
νόσκυα, οὐδὲν γὰρ ἔχει γλυκὺ ἐκεῖ να, τὰ κατὰ τοῦ Θεοῦ γινόμενα. κβʹ. Ὅταν δὲ
δοκῇ ἤδη πεπληρῶσθαι, θλι βήσεται, πᾶσα δὲ ἀνάγκη ἐπ' αὐτὸν ἐπε λεύσεται. Ταῦτά
φησιν· Ἕνεκα τῆς αἰτίας, ἀπόλ λυνται τὰ κτηθέντα, καὶ εἰς προγόνους οὐ
παραπέμπεται. κγʹ. Ἐπαποστείλαι ἐπ' αὐτὸν θυμὸν ὀργῆς, νίψαι ἐπ' αὐτὸν ὀδύνας.
Ἀντὶ τοῦ, ἐκ Θεοῦ καὶ ἐξ οὐρανοῦ ὑποσ τήσεται δεινά· ταῦτα δὲ ἔφη, ἐπειδὴ ὁ Ἰὼβ
φήσας ὑπὸ Θεοῦ πεπλῆχθαι, ἐμνημόνευσε καὶ ὡς ὑπὸ ἀνθρώπων ἠδικημένος· κατα
σκευάζει οὖν ὅτι πάντα δι' ἁμαρτίας ἐπ' αὐ τὸν ἐπηνέχθη. κεʹ. Ἄστρα δὲ ἐν διαίταις
pass_a_gloss: the mountains, so that he might say, not the things before the creation you know. Ch. 1, 17, 18. Earth, do not cover with the eyes of my flesh, nor let there be a place for my cry; and now behold in the heavens my witness, and my supporter in the highest. Wandering toward the earth he reasons, and calling for sympathy he says words, which also are well-spoken. And he says: Do not be silent, O earth, regarding me, nor secretly hide the unjustly shed blood from my flesh through the wounds; nor stand in a place and be hidden, nor let the things concerning my lamentations come into oblivion; many indeed, he says, were built up through my trials. Or let not the earth hide my blood, but let it call upon God for vengeance, having the wounds of the body as witnesses. And the air let not restrain my cry, but let the tone of the voice reach into the heavens, so that God of the happening evils may stand as avenger, and defending the guilty, thus indeed you will show to all the unblemished of my [actions]. And the: Behold in the heavens my witness, is purer than conscience. Ch. 19, 3. Know only that the Lord made me thus. To bring them into fear, such as one saying: Do not thus trample upon me suffering, nor may you yourselves fall into the same, having the same nature. 4, 5. Yes indeed upon truth I was led astray; but with me the deceiver mocks, to speak words which it was not necessary, and my words he wanders, and not in due time. – Let it be that upon me you magnify yourselves, and reproach me indeed. Let it be given, he says, according to the hypothesis that I was deceived. But with me the deceiver mocks; the deceiver the devil is. What harm, he says, to you from this, what necessity to judge as impious, and to trample upon one suffering?; it is necessary to sympathize with one speaking under pains. – If even such things he did such as were not necessary, 366 then was it necessary for you thus to reproach me?; – And it is necessary for me, he says, having long ago cared for piety, now to have the reputation from the works. This indeed I have not done, but I am judged as a deceiver. It imposes also here; 7. Know therefore that the Lord is the one who troubled; and his weapon upon me he raised up. Behold I will laugh at reproach, I will not speak. I have cried out, and nowhere [is] judgment. Reason with yourselves, he says; not from a purpose I am made, just as being encircled by some terrible wall. I speak, he says, with truth, how things are concerning me, and you do not accept the words. For it is in reproach, that he might say the things. And that I will not speak, instead of: because I think you oppose me to have said nothing at all. – If indeed even toward God I cry out, to make clearly known to all the things concerning me, I do not find favor. No one hears, no one judges, no one I see, I have nowhere to flee. These things are to be pitied, are they not? – For you indeed let go, thus unrighteously mocking me, lest God should establish himself for judgment, to execute upon you a sentence of irrational destruction. – For I do not flee, he says, God does not leave such things behind. It will be, he says, whether it be moved against you, as an unlearned opinion regarding the knowledge of the good appears to you, and regarding the things that are coming. – A. S. What do you say [that] being in wickedness I suffer these things, and you yourselves ought to fear the same. – Hurry then, he says, even while the things are testifying in words; therefore take hold of the words so that you might not be judged as unrighteous even by the truth. – The Hebrew indeed has a sin of the word. Ch. 21, 1. Having killed his sons, lesser ones, and his hands having burned the soles. 367 And those before, he says, more inferior, will cast down the children of the lawless. 14. Wealth being unjustly gathered will be examined, an angel will drag him out from his house. The impious indeed does all things so as to take others' things, and toward this man he looks at the purpose of the things happened; but when he seems master of all things, then he will see himself being carried away to others. 16. Like an unplowed plow, uncontrollable. The words and the doctrines [of the impious] are crooked and deceptive, for there is nothing sweet there, the things happening against God. 22. But when it seems already filled, it will be crushed, and all necessity will press upon him. These he says: Because of the cause, the acquired things are being stripped away, and to ancestors they are not being sent. 23. To send upon him a spirit of wrath, to pour upon him the soles. Instead of, he will undergo terrible things from God and from heaven; and these he said, since Job, having said he is struck by God, remembered also how he was wronged by men; therefore he prepares because all things through sin were brought upon him. 24. And stars in the diets...
pass_b_english: He appeals to the mountains, suggesting that they possess knowledge of things existing before the creation of the world [[Job 27:6 >> Bible:Job 27:6]]. In chapters 1, 17, and 18, he cries out, 'Earth, do not cover my eyes from my physical sight, nor let there be a place for my cry to echo; behold, my witness is in the heavens, and my supporter is in the highest heights.' As he wanders toward the earth, he reasons and calls out for sympathy, uttering words that are profoundly well-spoken. He says, 'O earth, do not remain silent regarding my plight, nor secretly conceal the blood unjustly shed from my flesh through my wounds; do not stand in a place and hide, nor let the memory of my lamentations fall into oblivion; for many have indeed been built up through my trials.' He continues, 'Let not the earth hide my blood, but let it summon God to vengeance, with the wounds of my body serving as witnesses. Let not the air restrain my cry, but let the sound of my voice reach the heavens, so that God, the avenger of these occurring evils, may stand forth. By defending the guilty, you will demonstrate to all the blamelessness of my conduct.' He adds, 'Behold, my witness in the heavens is purer than the human conscience' [[Job 19:3 >> Bible:Job 19:3]].

He instructs, 'Only know that the Lord has brought this upon me.' He speaks this to strike fear into them, saying, 'Do not trample upon me while I suffer, lest you yourselves fall into the same condition, sharing the same human nature' [[Job 4:5, 5:7 >> Bible:Job 4:5, 5:7]]. 'Truly, I have been led astray; yet the deceiver mocks me, speaking words that should never have been uttered, and he misrepresents my words and speaks them out of season. Let you magnify yourselves at my expense and reproach me. Let it be assumed, as a hypothesis, that I was deceived. But the deceiver mocks me; the deceiver is the devil. What harm comes to you from this? Why is it necessary to judge me as impious and to trample upon one in pain? It is necessary to show compassion to one speaking through agony.' He asks, 'If even such things were done that were not necessary, was it then necessary for you to reproach me so?' He says, 'Having long ago devoted myself to piety, it is necessary for me now to have a reputation based on my works. I have not done this, yet I am judged as a deceiver.' This applies here as well [[Job 7:6 >> Bible:Job 7:6]].

He declares, 'Know then that the Lord is the one who has troubled me; He has raised His weapon against me. Behold, I will laugh at your reproaches, but I will not speak. I have cried out, yet no judgment comes. Reason with yourselves; I am not made without purpose, though I feel as if I am encircled by a terrible wall. I speak the truth regarding my circumstances, yet you refuse to accept my words.' He explains that his refusal to speak is not because he has nothing to say, but rather because he feels that since you oppose me, it is better to remain silent. 'Even if I cry out to God to make my situation clear to everyone, I find no favor. No one listens, no one judges, I see no one, and I have nowhere to flee. Should these things not be pitied?' He suggests that by unrighteously mocking him, they allow God to stand as judge to execute a sentence of irrational destruction upon them. 'I do not flee,' he says, 'for God does not abandon such things.' He implies that what appears to you as an unlearned opinion regarding the knowledge of good and the things to come will eventually be proven true. He asks, 'What do you say to the fact that I suffer these things while in wickedness? You yourselves ought to fear the same.' He urges, 'Hurry, even while these things are testifying through words; grasp hold of the words so that you might not be judged as unrighteous even by the truth itself.'

The Hebrew text contains a sin of the word [[Job 21:1 >> Bible:Job 21:1]]. Having killed his lesser sons, and with his hands having burned the soles, he says those before him—those more inferior—will cast down the children of the lawless [[Job 14:14 >> Bible:Job 14:14]]. Wealth gathered unjustly will be scrutinized, and an angel will drag the man from his house. The impious man does everything to seize the possessions of others, and one looks at the purpose of these events through him; yet when he seems to be master of all, he will see himself being carried away to others [[Job 16:14 >> Bible:Job 16:14]]. Like an unplowed, uncontrollable plow, the words and doctrines of the impious are crooked and deceptive, for there is nothing sweet in things that happen against God [[Job 22:22 >> Bible:Job 22:22]]. But when he seems to be full, he will be crushed, and necessity will press upon him. He says that because of the cause, acquired things are being stripped away and will not be passed to his ancestors [[Job 23:12 >> Bible:Job 23:12]]. A spirit of wrath will be sent upon him to pour out his soles [[Job 23:16 >> Bible:Job 23:16]]. Instead, he will undergo terrible things from God and heaven. He said this because Job, having claimed he was struck by God, also remembered how he was wronged by men; thus, he prepares, knowing that all things were brought upon him through sin [[Job 24:24 >> Bible:Job 24:24]]. And stars in the diets...

choices.choice: The rewrite shifts from the literal, fragmented gloss to a cohesive narrative voice that captures Origen's explanatory tone, using 'He says' or 'He declares' to bridge the gap between the biblical quotes and the commentary.
